assumptions: Withdrawn relabel (r2 correction of the r1 asserted E=DOL claim): this record carries the operating-leverage-ratio value unchanged within the same CVP analysis and asserts no reading as price elasticity of demand. The r1 relabel is withdrawn because DOL (pct-change operating income over pct-change sales, CM/OI at the sales level) and price elasticity of demand (pct-change quantity over pct-change price from a demand curve) are distinct ratios, and CVP contains no demand curve from which bounded coincidence conditions could be derived.

Operating scope: above-break-even sales levels with positive net operating income (CM > FIX with FIX >= 0), so DOL = CM/(CM-FIX) >= 1 with equality iff FIX = 0; constant price, unit variable cost, mix and fixed expenses within the relevant range (ceteris paribus); a dimensionless ratio throughout.

Withdrawn relabel (r2 correction of the r1 asserted E=DOL claim): this record carries the operating-leverage-ratio value unchanged within the same CVP analysis and asserts no reading as price elasticity of demand. The r1 relabel is withdrawn because DOL (pct-change operating income over pct-change sales, CM/OI at the sales level) and price elasticity of demand (pct-change quantity over pct-change price from a demand curve) are distinct ratios, and CVP contains no demand curve from which bounded coincidence conditions could be derived.

Operating scope: above-break-even sales levels with positive net operating income (CM > FIX with FIX >= 0), so DOL = CM/(CM-FIX) >= 1 with equality iff FIX = 0; constant price, unit variable cost, mix and fixed expenses within the relevant range (ceteris paribus); a dimensionless ratio throughout.

Not a demand-elasticity estimate: the carried value must not be consumed as a price elasticity of demand; the registry signed point/midpoint elasticity records carry different meanings and do not bind here; any signed-elasticity use needs its own sign-convention record.

Below-break-even levels are excluded by the guard: zero or negative operating income cannot enter, including the CM=0 zero-contribution case (NOI=-FIX below break-even, or 0/0 if FIX=0); cross-analysis, cross-period, and rescaled uses are excluded.
